DroneOps Intelligence uses a Next.js/React Web application, an ASP.NET Core API, application services, EF Core/Npgsql persistence and PostgreSQL. A telemetry gateway supplies normalized MAVLink-derived samples, and SSE delivers authorized live updates. Backend adapters provide media storage, email and AI integration. Low-level UAV flight control remains external.

No | Component | Description | 1 | Next.js Web + proxy | Role-specific pages, client validation, map, same-origin forwarding. Backend remains authoritative for authorization and state. | 2 | API + Application | JWT/canonical roles, DTO validation, business services and outcome errors. Controllers delegate business operations to services; the composition root configures persistence and external adapters. | 3 | Persistence + Domain | EF entities/repositories plus Npgsql stores. Application depends on repository interfaces in Persistence and entities in Domain. | 4 | PostgreSQL / media | Transactional domain records; proposed request/evidence storage. Private user media uses protected backend read/upload and short-lived access; no public server secret. | 5 | Integration gateway / SSE | Normalized sample HTTP endpoint exists. Raw MAVLink adapter and background loss timer remain gaps; latest snapshot and SSE support frontend monitoring. | 6 | External AI / email | Configured outbound calls with bounded timeout, provenance and error handling. AI advice cannot approve missions.

The approval transaction checks the mission, request identity, record scope and current validation evidence before applying the accepted metadata and ordered waypoints. It records the decision and closes the request in the same transaction. Any failure rolls back the complete operation. Rejection updates only the request and decision, preserving current mission content and prior approval. A stale or conflicting request returns 409. Notification delivery follows the committed decision.

Indexes support ordered mission waypoints, pending requests, latest mission telemetry, incident status and recipient alerts. Ingestion uses an idempotency key, while decisions use a unique request identity and terminal-state check. Backend authorization protects mission, history, media and streaming operations.

This feature covers mission submission, pre-flight validation, proposed updates and Manager decisions. Approval applies accepted content to the same mission; rejection preserves current content and any existing approval.

PostFlightService provides history queries, report generation, telemetry playback, mission incidents and operational analytics. Aggregation uses authorized persisted samples and UTC coverage windows. Missing metrics remain null. Mission completion follows the external execution event; it is not a browser flight-control command.

Automatic flight preparation and workflow ownership

Current ownership: MF1 / WF-01 — NghiaHQ (Ha Quang Nghia), planning and preflight; MF2 / WF-02 — ThongLQ (Le Quoc Thong), realtime monitoring, incidents and flight preparation; MF3 / WF-03 — DucDDA (Dang Dao Anh Duc), post-flight; MF4 / WF-04 — KhanhGNG (Giang Nguyen Gia Khanh), AI assessment. ThongLQ remains team leader and dossier coordinator.

AutomaticFlightRequested is optional and defaults to false. Changes follow the mission proposal and approval workflow. This release prepares readiness; dispatchEnabled is false. Neither confirmation nor gateway enrollment uploads a mission, arms motors, sends TAKEOFF/AUTO/MISSION_START, or changes the mission to InProgress.

For an approved, opted-in mission with a schedule, the backend opens confirmation at T minus 5 minutes and closes it at the scheduled start. The authenticated operator must keep a visible browser tab online. Presence is sent every 10 seconds and expires after 30 seconds. The selected, unrevoked mission connection must match the active UAV and flight-controller UID, with gateway heartbeat within 30 seconds and telemetry within 15 seconds.

Confirmation reruns preflight and binds readiness to the exact plan hash and connection ID. Readiness requires a passing preflight for that hash from the last minute. Changed plan/connection, stale presence or missing telemetry invalidates the conditions; the operator must review and confirm again. Dismissal, a hidden/offline tab or a missed window is not flight consent.

Autopilot execution remains a separate development phase: firmware/airframe capability detection, mission compilation and upload/read-back, command IDs/deadlines and replay protection, scheduled condition rechecks, local pre-arm/failsafe enforcement, and ACK plus observed flight-state verification. Validate ArduPilot/PX4 SITL, propeller-free bench operation and supervised flight before enabling dispatch. AI advice cannot authorize launch.

MissionAutomationService and MissionAutomationController provide GET /api/missions/automation/due and GET /api/missions/{id}/automation, POST presence/confirm/cancel and GET plan below that mission automation route. Owner authorization and uav_operator role apply. MissionAutomationState retains presence/confirmation, confirmed plan hash and connection ID; trusted enrollment and mission leases remain separate. FlightPreparationPrompt polls only when visible/online. Migration: 20261104115300_gateway_enrollment_and_flight_preparation.sql; deploy backend, frontend and gateway package together.
